$comment: Copy to <project>/.claude/framework-manifest.json at install and fill it in. SETUP.md step 7 walks this.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The install RENAMES most of what it copies: stacks/<name>/ becomes
docs/stacks/<backend>/, modules/contracts/ becomes docs/contracts/, tooling/gate/gate-<stack>.sh becomes
gate.sh at each repo root, tooling/ci/<platform>/ becomes that platform's pipeline path. Nothing recorded those
renames, so /framework-upgrade could only resolve docs/process/ -- the one directory whose mapping is 1:1.
For everything else it had no way to know which upstream file an installed file came from, and the stack
identity was destroyed outright: once stacks/dotnet-api/ is called docs/stacks/<backend>/, nothing on disk
says it was dotnet-api. The upgrade silently skipped layer 2, the review templates, the gate scripts and
CI -- which is where all the editable content lives.
This file is the record. Every entry is one installed artifact and the upstream path it came from, so the
upgrade has a resolvable source for every target, /framework-doctor has a real layout check, and the
CHANGELOG's prose mapping table stops being load-bearing.
KEEP IT CURRENT. It is written at install and updated by /framework-upgrade. If you add a stack, add a
repo, or install an optional module later, add its entries here at the same time -- an entry that is
missing is a file the upgrade will not see.
The list NAMES ITSELF, on purpose. Without that entry the one file the upgrade reads to decide what it
may touch was the one file it could never resolve, so a change to the manifest's own shape -- a new
field, a renamed class -- was invisible to the mechanism that exists to surface changes.
$comment_answers: The SETUP answers that decide which files are installed and which rules apply. /framework-doctor reads these; keep them identical to the matching lines in CLAUDE.md.
$comment_forge: The hosting platform, from SETUP Q7. One of: github, gitlab, azure-devops, bitbucket.
It decides which CI wrapper and which code-ownership mechanism this project installed, and
/framework-upgrade needs it to know which upstream pipeline file an installed one came from.
review_evidence_cmd is the command Definition of Done item 6 accepts as proof that a human
approved the change request -- see tooling/ci/README.md for the per-platform forms. It lives here
as well as in CLAUDE.md because /framework-doctor checks the two agree; a project that answers this
question twice and differently has one answer nobody is reading.
$comment_stacks: Every stack this project installed, keyed by the ROLE it plays here. The installed directory is
docs/stacks/<the value>, so the folder is self-describing and the identity survives the install.
There is no fixed set of roles and no limit of two. The old layout offered exactly two slots --
docs/stack-backend/ and docs/stack-frontend/ -- and every cross-reference was written against those
names, so a project could install at most two stacks and they had to map onto a backend/frontend
dichotomy. A Python CLI, a Rust service, a Go binary, an iOS app, a data pipeline or a library fitted
neither slot; mobile + API + admin web was unrepresentable, and so was a monorepo with two backend
services. Add as many entries as the project has stacks, and name the roles after what they are.
$comment_repos: Repo-root-relative artifacts are installed once PER REPO. Single-repo projects list one entry with an empty path.
$comment_class: class matches the CHANGELOG's upgrade actions and decides what an upgrade may do without asking:
copy    layer 1/2 doc. The project never edits it, so replace outright. Drift here is a finding.
merge   the project edited this at install (gate commands, filled placeholders). NEVER overwrite;
the upgrade quotes the upstream change for a human to apply.
local   generated at install from a template and owned by the project from then on. The upgrade
reports upstream changes but does not touch the file.
$comment_files: Two lists, because the install has two shapes. `files` is installed ONCE per project. `per_repo_files`
is installed once per entry in `repos` above, with {{REPO_DIR}} standing for that repo's path and
`files` used to carry the gate and the stub ratchet under fixed {{BACKEND_DIR}} and {{FRONTEND_DIR}}
slots, which contradicted `repos` being an array and `$comment_stacks` saying there is no limit of two.
A third repo got no manifest entry for its gate, so /framework-upgrade skipped it in silence -- which is
the exact failure this file exists to end. Expand per_repo_files per repo when you write the manifest,
or leave the placeholders and let /framework-upgrade expand them against `repos`.
Conditionally-installed files are listed ONE PER FILE, never as a directory. process/optional/ was a
single `copy` entry for three files that SETUP installs independently (Q2, multi-agent use, and a
placeholder you may skip), so the manifest asserted a directory the project does not have. Delete the
lines this project did not install.
$comment_per_repo: Installed once PER ENTRY in repos[]. Expand it per repo, replacing {{REPO_DIR}} with that repo's path
and {{REPO_STACK_FAMILY}} with its gate family. A single-repo project expands it once with an empty path.
CI LIVES HERE, NOT IN files[]. The pipeline runs where the code is, so a multi-repo project needs one
pipeline per code repo -- and while these entries sat in files[] a project got exactly one, for whichever
repo happened to be first. The wrapper is thin; gate-ci.sh carries every check, so BOTH are per-repo and
both must be present. A repo with the wrapper and no script has a pipeline that cannot run; a repo with
the script and no wrapper has a gate nothing invokes.
{{FORGE}} is the platform from SETUP Q7; {{CI_WRAPPER_FILE}} and {{CI_WRAPPER_INSTALLED}} follow from it:
github        gate.yml                   -> .github/workflows/gate.yml
gitlab        .gitlab-ci.yml             -> .gitlab-ci.yml
azure-devops  azure-pipelines.yml        -> azure-pipelines.yml
bitbucket     bitbucket-pipelines.yml    -> bitbucket-pipelines.yml
{{OWNERSHIP_FILE}} / {{OWNERSHIP_INSTALLED}} likewise, and only two platforms have a FILE:
github        CODEOWNERS  -> .github/CODEOWNERS
gitlab        CODEOWNERS  -> CODEOWNERS        (Premium only -- see the file)
azure-devops  no file exists. DELETE the ownership entry and configure branch policies instead.
bitbucket     no file exists. DELETE the ownership entry and configure branch restrictions instead.
Deleting the entry on those two platforms is correct, not a shortcut: a manifest that claims a file which
is not there makes /framework-doctor report a phantom problem, and a check that reports phantom problems
is one people learn to ignore. Record the decision in CLAUDE.md so the gap is documented rather than lost.
$comment_omitted: Delete every entry above that this project did not install -- an optional layer-1 document it skipped, a
second stack it does not have, the .ps1 gates on a POSIX-only team. A manifest that claims files which
are not there makes /framework-doctor report phantom problems, and a check that reports phantom problems
is one people learn to ignore.
